title: The Rough Summit
premise: Ivo Villalobos, a salvage diver drowning in debt, is salvaging a wreck the navy forbids her to discuss when a low tide exposes a sea cave holding a dead climber, an antique compass matching her own, and a map to a summit cache left by the legendary expedition that vanished forty years ago. Hunted by the navy officer who wants the cave erased and by the dead man's heirs who want the inheritance, Ivo assembles a ragged team — a disgraced glaciologist, a washed-out mountain guide, and the heir who betrayed his own family to find it — and races across the range ahead of the snows. At the calving glacier's brief opening, she learns the 'treasure' is evidence: proof the original expedition was murdered to bury a mining company's crimes, with her own grandfather among the killers. In the end Ivo chooses found family over blood and fortune, publishing the truth and walking away from the summit with the people who climbed beside her.
about_author: Ansel Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines from Norway to Patagonia before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose loyalties are tested by weather, water, and money.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Diving a navy-sealed wreck to pay her debts, she notices the tide has dropped impossibly low, revealing a cave mouth on the cliff below the old lighthouse. Inside she finds a frozen-preserved corpse in vintage climbing gear clutching a compass identical to hers — her grandfather's make, her family's engraving. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread; she takes the compass and tells no one.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Wrecks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Navy Lieutenant Casals summons her, offering to erase her debt if she surrenders what she took from the cave — revealing he knows exactly what's inside. She lies. That night someone ransacks her boat, and a stranger named Teo Abarca catches her at gunpoint, claiming the dead man was his uncle and the compass is his inheritance. Beat: Ivo realizes she's caught between two predators and chooses neither.

chapters.title: A Team of Last Resorts
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Reluctant allies, they recruit Dr. Sunniva Rask, a glaciologist blacklisted for insisting the calving season will open the high route weeks early, and Marisol Quen, a guide banned after a client died. Each joins for their own debt or disgrace. Around a harbor fire they study the map hidden in the compass lid: a route to the summit cache. Beat: four broken people agreeing to one impossible climb.

chapters.title: The Navy's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The team slips out of port ahead of a storm, but Casals anticipates them — he wants the cave's contents buried because his own career was built on the cover-up. A near-arrest at the coastal checkpoint forces them inland on foot, days behind schedule. Beat: the race becomes real; trust is tested when Ivo admits she kept the second compass for herself.

chapters.title: Treeline
chapters.summary: Sunniva's POV. The forest gives way to scree and the first signs that the original expedition came this way: a rusted piton line, a grave marker with five names but six sets of gear tracks. Sunniva reads the ice like text and warns the calving window is shrinking. Teo grows secretive about what his uncle's letters promised. Beat: awe shadowed by the sense of being followed by history itself.

chapters.title: The Col
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A whiteout traps them two days in a snow cave, where rationed air forces confessions: Marisol's client death was sabotage by a rival guide paid by the same mining company; Teo's uncle didn't die on the mountain — he was pushed. Ivo reveals her grandfather led the original expedition. Beat: the group fractures along the fault line of inheritance versus loyalty.

chapters.title: Icefall Crossing
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The calving season opens early, exactly as Sunniva predicted — the glacier groans apart just long enough to expose the route. They cross under collapsing seracs while Casals's hired climbers close in behind. Marisol saves Teo from a crevasse at the cost of the rope, the radio, and nearly herself. Beat: terror transmuted into the first real bond between them.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. At the summit shelter they find the cache: not gold, but documents, photographs, and a confession naming the mining company and its navy protectors — including the signature of Ivo's grandfather ordering the sixth member's death. Casals arrives with his climbers and offers everyone a share to burn it. Beat: betrayal crystallizes; Teo must choose revenge against Ivo or truth with her.

chapters.title: Rough Summit
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Storm and gunfire on the summit ridge. Casals falls to his death reaching for the documents he can't let go of; his hired climbers, seeing the evidence, refuse to fight. Ivo confronts her grandfather's ghost in the pages of his own confession and chooses to carry the shame rather than inherit the silence. Beat: climax — power's corruption exposed at the top of the world.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Shared POV, rotating per section. The four descend together through the closing window, publishing the evidence from a valley town where the signal finally reaches. The navy's cover-up collapses; the debts dissolve in scandal rather than payment. Ivo keeps neither compass nor fortune, only the team. Final image: the tide giving back nothing at all, and Ivo not needing it to. Beat: resolution — found family as the only inheritance worth keeping.
